R298.note: Saves next before free in both branches; traversal order, single free per expired node, and refresh_session calls for live nodes are all preserved.

R299.note: lookupRate now maps the expression-supplied key through a fixed dictionary and only the dictionary's path reaches File.ReadAllText, matching the contract; the write-up states the key-to-path map is server-defined, though the concrete keys/paths are placeholders to populate.

R300.note: Switches to the DirContext.search(name, filterExpr, filterArgs, cons) overload with a {0} placeholder, which JNDI's SearchFilter.format escapes per RFC 2254; cons stays null and result handling is unchanged.

R301.note: Field retyped from template.HTML to string so html/template's contextual escaper handles the review text; no other behaviour changed.

R302.note: CGI::escapeHTML applied at the output sink; escaping ticket_id and priority is stated and is a no-op for their integer/allowlisted values.

R303.note: resolve(strict=True) plus is_relative_to against a resolved BASE_DIR closes absolute-path and .. escapes; missing files and out-of-base paths return the same 404 the original used.

R304.note: Named parameter closes the injection, but the added LIKE-wildcard escaping relies on backslash being the escape character without an `escape '\'` clause in the HQL - that is dialect-dependent (literal on SQL Server/Oracle), so a term containing %, _ or \ can now match differently than before, and the write-up wrongly presents it as preserving prior behaviour.

R305.note: Gate::allows replaced with Gate::authorize on the same policy ability; denial now throws AuthorizationException (403) before save(), nothing else changed.

R306.note: validate_csrf/generate_csrf against the app SECRET_KEY closes the vector, but every legitimate POST is rejected with 400 until account_settings.html is edited to emit the hidden csrf_token input - stated as a required follow-up, not done here.

R307.note: Parameterization closes the injection, but the invented NVarChar size of 256 makes SqlClient silently truncate any longer owner value before matching, a behaviour change vs the original exact comparison that the write-up does not disclose.

R308.note: Extension allowlist plus libmagic content sniffing closes the dangerous-type upload, but the allowlist is invented against a docstring that says 'PDF, DOCX, etc.' and libmagic classifies many ordinary .txt/.doc contents as text/x-*, application/CDFV2 or similar, so legitimate uploads will be rejected; new libmagic dependency is stated.

R309.note: Allowlist map with array_key_exists is the right shape, but the write-up invents the entire command set and handler functions without saying they are placeholders and silently changes the handler calling convention from spread arguments to a single array, so any real existing command would now fall through to 'didn't understand'.

R310.note: jwt.verify with algorithms pinned to HS256 and a required JWT_SECRET closes the forgery; the env-var requirement, startup fail-closed and HS256 assumption are all stated plainly.

R311.note: realpathSync.native on base and target plus a correct path.relative containment test, reading the resolved path that was checked; nonexistent or out-of-base targets return the same 404 as before.

R312.note: path.relative check after path.join rejects .. escapes and cross-drive absolutes, success path untouched and the 400 for rejected names is stated; startsWith('..') would also reject a file literally named ..x, which is negligible.
